clue.text: Something attractive, foremost of gardens captured by French painter

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece goes within the other
foremost picks out the very front of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A lovely garden view painted by a French artist is the thing that draws the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is anything, or anyone, that draws people towards it, a figurative sense of the iron-pulling object.

clue.text: Strength of beast of burden carrying spades about

indicators.note: an animal carrying a load holds it within, so these letters go inside the beast

parts.note: a mule is a pack animal
S is the card abbreviation for spades
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A pack animal's power as it carries garden spades around.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is used loosely for physical power or force, as in 'putting some muscle into it'.

clue.text: Good boy getting fourteen pounds from former PM

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a stone is a British unit of weight equal to fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A well-behaved youngster receiving a heavy sum from a one-time Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is the British weight unit still used for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone served four times as British Prime Minister in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Type of grass found in part of Pyrenees? Part of

indicators.note: found in tells you the word is sitting within the following run of letters

parts.note: the tail of the mountain range's name runs on into the next two words

explanation.surface: A botanist wonders whether a certain grass grows in a stretch of the Pyrenees.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Part of' is wordplay text, not a repeat: its letters complete the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish and North African grass used for making rope, paper and baskets.

clue.text: Operator needs a fresh start and to develop quickly

indicators.note: a fresh start means swapping the opening letter of the word for a different one

explanation.surface: A worker in need of a new beginning who wants to progress fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the S, so the definition settles it: B gives the word meaning to grow fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow or expand rapidly, like buds putting out shoots.

clue.text: Large young lady's shirt-like garment is wet

parts.note: a girl is a young lady, with the possessive kept
a blouse is a woman's shirt

explanation.surface: A tall girl's top has been soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is the British noun for a feeble, ineffectual person, not the adjective the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Big girl's blouse is British slang for a weak or timid man, the same as calling him a wet.

clue.text: Warm coastal district in Rhode Island, one crossed by girl

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

indicators.note: something crossed by another has it running through its middle, so one piece sits inside

explanation.surface: A sunny shore in Rhode Island where a girl crosses someone's path.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the sunny Mediterranean coast of France and Italy, and by extension any warm resort coastline.

clue.text: Former partner on craft coming over more

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: coming over suggests turning back on itself, so the word is read from the end

explanation.surface: An ex arrives by boat, and there's more to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Unnecessary to pierce ends of sacs

parts.note: to needle is to prick or pierce

indicators.note: ends of points to the first and last letters of the next word only

parts.note: the two end letters of sacs

explanation.surface: There's no need to puncture the ends of sacs.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless is a synonym for unnecessary, as in a needless risk.

clue.text: Expose a wrongdoing, as a referee will

definitions.meaning: first meaning: inform on wrongdoing inside an organisation

definitions.note: describes the action rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what an official literally does to stop play

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally: a referee sounds a whistle to stop the game for a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to report misconduct publicly, and literally describes a referee signalling an infringement.

clue.text: Knife left in various places

indicators.note: various suggests a mixture of forms, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A blade has been left lying around in several spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small, very sharp knife used by surgeons.

clue.text: Allowed to hold outrageous dance

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: gave as in gave permission, allowed
OTT is short for over the top, outrageous

explanation.surface: Permission granted for a scandalous dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French court dance in moderate four-four time.

clue.text: No-hoper's not as far away once leader's fallen

indicators.note: the leader falling away means the word's opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A hopeless runner is nearer the front only after the race leader has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails, a person with no hope of success.

clue.text: The British government will, Heath worried

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and worked over, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: The government will carry on, Prime Minister Edward Heath fretting about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British Conservative Prime Minister in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is the London street of ministries, used as shorthand for the British civil service and government.

clue.text: Novelist's Tory lord — he's cracked cases put into words

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the scrambled letters wrap round another piece
something cracked is broken up, so these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: to say is to express in words

explanation.surface: A writer's Conservative peer has cracked and is spelling out his case.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L Sayers was the English writer of the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels.

clue.text: Holly's one song that's been popular for a long time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plant that keeps its leaves all year, as holly does

definitions.text: song that's been popular for a long time
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a tune that never goes out of fashion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holly' looks like a singer such as Buddy Holly, which feeds the song idea; it is the shrub, and 'Holly's one' means holly is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a plant in leaf all year and, figuratively, a perennially popular song or show.

clue.text: What can make borders ultimately neater?

definitions.text: What can make borders ultimately neater?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A gardener asks what tool would tidy up the flower beds' edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: this garden tool is what makes the edges of beds tidier.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a British name for a powered line trimmer used to cut grass along edges.

clue.text: Louis and former PM in the joint

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other, here within the last two words

parts.note: Gordon Brown, British Prime Minister 2007 to 2010
a bomber is slang for a large cannabis joint

explanation.surface: Louis and a former Prime Minister are sharing a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis is Joe Louis, the boxer, not a French king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brown Bomber was the nickname of Joe Louis, world heavyweight boxing champion from 1937 to 1949.

clue.text: Cat and dog injured during short demo

indicators.note: during places one thing inside the time span of another, so it goes within
short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rally is a protest gathering, a demo

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat and a dog got hurt at a brief protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ragdoll is a large, docile breed of domestic cat that goes limp when picked up.

clue.text: Be hooked by new form of match play

indicators.note: something hooked is caught and held, so it ends up inside the other piece
a new form means the same letters given a different shape

explanation.surface: Get hooked on a novel way of playing a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's tragedy of a Scottish king's murderous ambition.

clue.text: Attempt to secure object with it

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the other piece is held inside

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Try to fasten the item with it.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is an idiom for fashionable, which is exactly what trendy means.

clue.text: On the sly, poured out gin and tonic, nothing more

indicators.note: something poured out is spilled and loses its shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone secretly fixes a gin and tonic and stops at just the one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' only joins the two drinks; the extra nothing is added to the mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito means in disguise or unrecognised, acting secretly.

clue.text: Savoury food in bars

definitions.meaning: first meaning: patties such as fishcakes or crab ...
second meaning: solid blocks, as of soap

explanation.surface: Snacks served in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs, but it means blocks, as in cakes of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishcakes and potato cakes are savoury patties, and a block of soap is a cake of soap.

clue.text: Soldier returning in vehicle points to smoke

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier coming home in his car gestures towards the smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is a roll of tobacco leaves for smoking, a smoke in casual speech.

clue.text: Manage to see fashion abroad

parts.note: abroad as in out and about, outside

explanation.surface: Struggling to spot the trends overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to discern it with difficulty, just barely see it.

clue.text: Spotted entertaining ambassador and bishop in an unlicensed establishment

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An envoy and a cleric were seen drinking at an illegal bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an Irish, Scottish or South African term for an illicit drinking den.

clue.text: Willpower about to crack

parts.note: to crack a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: Someone's determination is on the point of breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is firmness of purpose, the determination that willpower provides.

clue.text: Suspicious about new drink

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the other

explanation.surface: Wary of a newly introduced drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a common British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer.
